issues.t: Automatic slips and the O/D light flashes
issues.sym: The truck flares in RPM between gears, gets stuck in second or third, shifts late, or won't climb a hill in reverse. The overdrive (O/D) light on the dash blinks. Shutting the engine off sometimes clears it for a while.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic in the first-generation Sport Trac is the most-reported trouble spot for these years. Internal wear, torque converter failure and shift solenoid problems lead to slipping, and the computer flashes the O/D light when it sees a transmission fault. Most reports land between about 60,000 and 110,000 miles.
issues.next: A flashing O/D light means the transmission computer has stored a fault, so have the codes read soon. Check the fluid level and color. Avoid towing or hard driving until it is diagnosed, because slipping quickly makes the damage worse. Many trucks end up needing a rebuild.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails on 2007-2010 trucks
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs, a sudden loss of drive, or a shift into the wrong gear while accelerating. Some trucks lose forward and reverse completely and have to be towed.
issues.why: Owners of second-generation trucks with both the V6 and the V8 report complete transmission failures, often between 75,000 and 110,000 miles. Reported causes include a failed torque converter that sends metal through the unit, worn shift servo bores in the case and damaged shift solenoids.
issues.next: If the truck slips or loses a gear, stop towing and get the transmission scanned and the fluid checked right away. Ask the shop for a written diagnosis before agreeing to a rebuild, and ask Ford whether any extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or failure
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter from the engine, loudest for a few seconds after a cold start, that gets worse over time. It may come with a check engine light. If a chain or guide breaks, the engine can stop running.
issues.why: The 4.0L overhead-cam V6 uses several timing chains with plastic guides and tensioners. The guides crack and the tensioners wear, so the chains slap. A broken guide can punch through the valve cover, and a broken chain can damage the engine.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new rattle. Have a shop listen to it and check for cam timing codes. Replacing the chains, guides and tensioners before something breaks can save the engine.

issues.t: Harsh, delayed or slamming shifts
issues.sym: The truck jerks or bangs into gear at low speed, slams into reverse, pauses a few seconds before engaging, or shudders when pulling away.
issues.why: Owners trace this to transmission computer programming, the solenoid pack, or chafed transmission wiring. Ford issued a service bulletin (8-4-16 is cited by owners) that reprograms the computer for this complaint.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check for transmission software updates and service bulletins for your VIN before replacing parts. If shifts keep getting worse or the truck slips, have it diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: No-crank or stalling from chafed engine computer wiring
issues.sym: The engine won't crank, stalls, runs poorly, or the check engine light comes on, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: Ford service bulletins for these trucks describe the engine wiring harness rubbing against the engine computer (PCM) mounting bracket, and other no-crank and drivability faults tied to the engine and transmission computers.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and inspect the harness at the PCM bracket for rubbed-through wires. Mention the Ford bulletins so they look there first.

issues.t: Hard starting, rough idle or idle dips when slowing
issues.sym: Long cranking before it starts, rough running, or the idle dropping very low (below about 600 rpm) as you coast to a stop.
issues.why: Ford service bulletin 08-9-5 covers 4.0L and 4.6L trucks built on or before April 2, 2008 for this complaint, which is fixed with updated engine computer software.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check whether bulletin 08-9-5 applies to your truck and whether the software update has been done.

issues.t: Spark plugs break off during removal
issues.sym: During a tune-up, one or more spark plugs snap and leave part of the plug stuck in the cylinder head. The truck may have been in for a misfire.
issues.why: The 3-valve V8 used a two-piece spark plug whose lower shell can seize in the aluminum head with carbon. Ford bulletin 08-7-6 covers 2007-2008 Sport Trac V8s built before November 30, 2007 and gives a special cold-engine removal procedure.
issues.next: Have plugs changed by a shop that knows Ford's procedure and has the extraction tools. Never remove them with the engine warm. Ask for a quote that covers broken-plug extraction before work starts.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley rubber separates
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or rubbing sound from the front of the engine, often worse when wet or with the A/C on. The belt may shred. In bad cases the pulley comes apart and the engine stalls or won't start.
issues.why: The crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) has a rubber ring between its hub and outer belt ring. When the rubber breaks down, the outer ring slips or wobbles and chews up the drive belt.
issues.next: If you hear a new belt noise, have the crank pulley checked for wobble or a cracked rubber ring before replacing just the belt. Get it fixed soon: if the pulley lets go, you lose the alternator and water pump drive.

issues.t: Radiator cracks at the plastic top tank
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, coolant puddles under the front, a dropping coolant level, or the temperature gauge swinging toward hot.
issues.why: The radiator's plastic top tank can split, often right under the coolant overflow area. Owners report it from about 27,000 to 130,000 miles.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and shut off the engine. Don't open a hot cap. Check under the truck and around the radiator top for wet coolant, and replace the radiator before driving far.

issues.t: Plastic thermostat housing cracks and leaks
issues.sym: Coolant seeping or dripping near the top front of the engine, a low coolant level, or a coolant smell after driving.
issues.why: The thermostat housing on the V6 is plastic and can crack. Owners have replaced it with an aluminum aftermarket housing.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the housing replaced soon. Watch the temperature gauge; if it climbs, pull over and let the engine cool.

issues.t: Cab-to-frame body mounts crumble
issues.sym: Rattling or tapping from the floor, more body lean in turns, or the cab feeling loose on the frame. In severe cases there is a loud pop and the hood no longer lines up.
issues.why: The rubber bushings that hold the cab to the frame rot and break apart with age, usually past 80,000 to 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the body mounts inspected from underneath. Replace them as a set with new hardware; rusted bolts may add labor.

issues.t: Paint cracking or peeling on hood and cab
issues.sym: Fine spiderweb cracks or peeling in the paint and clear coat on the hood, roof and fenders.
issues.why: Owners of early trucks report widespread paint cracking, often by about 45,000 miles. Ford did not give one cause; some trucks were repainted under warranty when new.
issues.next: This is cosmetic, but bare metal can rust. Get a body shop quote, and touch up any spots down to metal to slow rust.

issues.t: Four-wheel drive will not engage
issues.sym: Pressing the 4x4 switch does nothing: the 4x4 light stays off and the truck stays in two-wheel drive.
issues.why: Owners trace it to a burned-out transfer case shift motor or a corroded wiring connection at the 4x4 solenoid.
issues.next: Try it on a straight road at low speed. If it still won't engage, have a shop test the switch, wiring and shift motor before replacing parts. Don't count on 4x4 in snow until it's fixed.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints wear out
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: Owners of early trucks report worn front lower ball joints. A worn joint loosens the steering and, if ignored, can fail.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play at the next tire rotation. Replace worn ball joints promptly and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Gauges and instrument cluster cut out
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel and temperature gauges read wrong, freeze or die, sometimes along with the odometer and warning lights. It may work one day and not the next.
issues.why: The instrument cluster itself fails internally. Shops usually replace or rebuild the cluster.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Don't rely on the fuel gauge; reset the trip meter at each fill-up. Have the cluster tested, and ask about a rebuilt unit as an option to new.

issues.t: Oil seepage at the rear axle shaft seals
issues.sym: Oily residue near the rear wheels or on the inside of the rear tires.
issues.why: Ford service bulletin 08-19-3 notes that oil can separate from the axle shaft cartridge seal and is often mistaken for an axle gear oil leak.
issues.next: Have the shop check the bulletin before replacing axle parts. Check that the rear axle oil level is correct; a true leak onto the brakes needs prompt repair.

issues.t: Front brake rotors and calipers wear out early
issues.sym: Pulsing in the brake pedal, grinding, or uneven pad wear well before 30,000 miles.
issues.why: An owner reports repeated early front rotor and caliper failures, which a technician blamed on the original parts; Ford reimbursed the repairs. Ford also issued bulletin 08-2-8 for brake pedal feel on these trucks.
issues.next: If the pedal pulses or you hear grinding, have the brakes inspected now. Keep records, and ask a Ford dealer whether goodwill coverage is possible on low mileage.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor fails
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on or the passenger airbag shows as off when someone is sitting there.
issues.why: The passenger-side airbag sensor can fail internally, leaving the passenger airbag disabled.
issues.next: Treat the airbag light as urgent: the airbag may not deploy in a crash. Have the SRS codes read, and keep children in the back seat until it's repaired.

issues.t: Water leaks into the rear cab area
issues.sym: Water in the rear storage tray or behind the rear seat after rain, wet seatbacks, or a musty smell.
issues.why: Owners were told water gets in around the rear light assemblies; resealing or replacing the lamp assembly is the usual fix.
issues.next: Dry the area out to stop mold. Have the lamp seals and other openings water-tested, then reseal the source.

issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it happens. Smoke or flames may appear under the hood near the brake master cylinder.
issues.why: The speed control deactivation switch on the brake master cylinder can fail and start an underhood fire. Recall 07V-336 covers these trucks.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If it hasn't been done, have a Ford dealer do it free, and park away from buildings until then.

issues.t: Firestone tires can lose their tread (recall)
issues.sym: A thumping or vibration at speed, a bulge in the tire, or sudden tread loss on the highway.
issues.why: Firestone Wilderness AT tires fitted to many Ford trucks could separate at highway speed. Recall 01X-001 replaced them.
issues.next: Any truck this age should be on newer tires, but check the sidewalls. If you find Wilderness AT tires, replace them right away.

issues.t: Hood can fly up while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood may pop up at speed and block your view.
issues.why: Recall 00V-394 addressed hoods that could fly up while the truck was moving.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done with your VIN. Always make sure the hood is fully latched after checking the oil.

issues.t: Throttle may not return to idle after cruise control (recall)
issues.sym: When you cancel cruise control, the engine may keep pulling instead of dropping to idle. Braking still works, but stopping takes longer.
issues.why: The speed control cable could bind so the throttle return spring can't close the throttle. Recall 03V-280 fixed it.
issues.next: If the engine keeps pulling, brake firmly and shift to neutral. Confirm the recall was done with your VIN.

issues.t: Front seatbacks may fold back in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: Under recall 03V-281, the high-back front seats could move rearward in some crashes, so the driver could lose contact with the steering wheel and pedals.
issues.next: Look up your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have any open recall done free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Amber side reflectors may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: The amber side reflectors may be missing, which makes the truck harder to see from the side at night.
issues.why: Recall 06E-026 covered trucks fitted with lamp parts that lacked the required amber side reflectors.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check this recall with your VIN and replace the parts if needed.

issues.t: Fuel line connection can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell, or fuel dripping under the truck.
issues.why: Recall 06E-056 covered a fuel connection that could fail and leak fuel, creating a fire risk near any ignition source.
issues.next: If you smell gas, don't start or drive the truck; have it towed. Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

issues.t: Steering gear can clunk and lose effectiveness (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk when turning the steering wheel, or steering that feels less precise.
issues.why: Recall 07V-181 covered a small batch of trucks whose steering gear assembly could clunk and lose steering effectiveness.
issues.next: Have any steering clunk checked right away, and run your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Red transmission fluid dripping under the truck, or a burning smell or smoke from underneath.
issues.why: Under recall 07V-453, the bolt holding a transmission cooler line may not have been tightened properly. Leaking fluid can hit the catalytic converter and start a fire.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over and shut off the engine. Check your VIN for open recalls and have it fixed free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Front seat recliners may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving; rarely, a seatback that feels loose.
issues.why: Under recall 10V-161, the manual recliners on the front seats could let the seatback and head restraint move rearward in a crash.
issues.next: Look up your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the free repair done at a Ford dealer.
